clue.text: One who goes to work on foot

definitions.text: One who goes to work on foot

parts.words: One who goes to work on foot
parts.note: reads like a commuter who walks to the office, but means a professional whose work is done on people's feet

explanation.surface: A commuter who walks to the office every morning.
explanation.definitionFit: A podiatrist treats ailments of the feet, so the foot is literally the material worked on.

clue.text: Linesman, a flighty creature that can find its way back from distant places

definitions.meaning: the Greek poet of the Iliad was a man who wrote lines of verse

definitions.text: a flighty creature that can find its way back from distant places
definitions.meaning: a pigeon trained to fly home

explanation.definitionFit: Homer is the epic poet, a writer of lines; a homer is also a homing pigeon.

clue.text: In a hurry hoping to be elected?

explanation.definitionFit: Someone dashing is moving quickly on foot; a candidate is said to stand for office.

clue.text: Quite a lot of cigarettes

definitions.meaning: a large sum, as in 'it cost a ...'
the small box in which cigarettes are sold

explanation.definitionFit: Slang uses the word for a large sum of money; it is also the box cigarettes come in.

clue.text: Kenneth risked going out as it became more gloomy

indicators.note: the word for risked goes outside, around the short name

parts.note: to dare is to risk, so risked is dared
Ken is short for Kenneth

explanation.surface: Kenneth took a chance by leaving the house as the sky grew dark.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that darkened grew dimmer or more sombre in light or mood.

clue.text: Fruit prepared as a must

indicators.note: the letters of 'as a must' are prepared, made up afresh in a new order

explanation.surface: Fruit gets prepared because it is essential.
explanation.definitionFit: A satsuma is a small, loose-skinned citrus fruit like a tangerine.

clue.text: When the fat catches fire it don't long

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held reads 'When the fat catches fire it don't long': a word is missing (probably 'doesn't last long'), and no scan or search gives the printed text.
annotationWithheld.clue: When the fat catches fire it don't long

clue.text: Staff needed for anatomy lectures

parts.note: staff suggests personnel, recalling a minimal crew, while the anatomy class needs the bony frame of a body on display

explanation.surface: A medical school needs employees to run its anatomy course.
explanation.definitionFit: A skeleton staff is a minimal crew, and the bony frame of a body is used to teach anatomy.

clue.text: Is it an advantage of working in a hair salon

definitions.text: Is it an advantage of working in a hair salon

parts.words: Is it an advantage of working in a hair salon
parts.note: a workplace perk, punning on the hairstyle of a cut across the forehead

explanation.surface: Someone wonders what perks a hairdresser's job brings.
explanation.definitionFit: A perk given on top of wages, punning on the cut of hair across the forehead.

clue.text: Fruit tart

definitions.meaning: sharp or sour in taste, as a citrus can be

explanation.definitionFit: The citrus is a fruit, and its sour taste makes it a byword for something tart.

clue.text: He is not employed to mind his own business

definitions.text: He is not employed to mind his own business

parts.words: He is not employed to mind his own business
parts.note: sounds like a busybody's motto, but describes a worker paid to look after property that belongs to someone else

explanation.surface: A nosy man who cannot keep out of other people's affairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A janitor or custodian looks after a building owned by others, minding their business rather than his.

clue.text: Divination, kind that is to include member

parts.note: a kind is a sort

indicators.note: the abbreviation for 'that is' is made to take another piece within it

parts.note: i.e. is the Latin abbreviation for 'that is'
a leg is a limb, a member of the body

explanation.surface: A fortune-teller describes a kind of divination that takes in a limb.
explanation.definitionFit: Sortilege is fortune-telling by drawing lots, a form of divination.

clue.text: Hal accidentally caught by a European mounted lancer

indicators.note: the jumbled name is held inside the European word, caught between its letters

parts.note: un is French for 'a', the word a European on the Continent would use

indicators.note: the name Hal is scrambled as if by accident

explanation.surface: A man called Hal is accidentally arrested by a European cavalryman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a European' stands for the French indefinite article, the word for 'a' across the Channel; 'accidentally' jumbles the name and 'caught by' sets it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An uhlan was a cavalryman armed with a lance in the Polish, German and Austrian armies.

clue.text: Call to question the little devil playing with the gun

parts.note: an imp is a small devil

indicators.note: the word gun is played about with, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone challenges a naughty child who is fooling around with a firearm.
explanation.definitionFit: To impugn a claim is to challenge it or call its truth into question.

clue.text: Fighting an opponent ofit

parts.note: reads as a boxer facing someone, but means a person opposed to fighting itself

explanation.surface: A combatant squares up to a rival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ofit' is 'of it' run together in the print.
explanation.definitionFit: One who believes war and violence are wrong is opposed to all combat.

clue.text: Witty retort coming from the pear-tree

indicators.note: the answer's letters come out of the words pear-tree once they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A clever remark is heard from up a fruit tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Repartee is quick, witty conversation full of sharp comebacks.

clue.text: Aim to achieve perfection

parts.note: sounds like an aspiration, but alludes to the saying that repetition makes perfect

explanation.surface: Someone sets the goal of becoming flawless.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'practice makes perfect' gives the verb, here in the British spelling with S.
explanation.definitionFit: Repeated rehearsal is the way, according to the proverb, to become perfect.

clue.text: Go after Act I curiously saying little

indicators.note: the second piece is placed after the first
the letters of Act I are arranged in a curious, odd way

parts.note: a go is a turn, as in a game

explanation.surface: A taciturn player takes their go after the first act of a play.
explanation.definitionFit: A taciturn person is reserved and speaks very little.

clue.text: Is a unit to be reformed in Africa

indicators.note: the letters of 'is a unit' are re-formed into a new shape

explanation.surface: A military unit is due to be reorganised in Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Tunisia is a North African country, so it is one place found there.

clue.text: Meeting Irish boy in front of church

parts.note: Sean is an Irish boy's name
CE stands for Church of England

explanation.surface: An Irish lad has an appointment outside the church.
explanation.definitionFit: A seance is a sitting or gathering held to contact the dead.

clue.text: Unearths old shades, about 1,000

parts.note: ex means former or old

indicators.note: the colour word goes around the Roman numeral

parts.note: hues are shades of colour
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: Someone digs up old tints worth around a thousand.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhume is to dig a body out of the ground, to unearth it.

clue.text: Accent on footwear

definitions.meaning: a strong regional accent, especially Irish
a stout leather shoe with decorative perforations

explanation.definitionFit: A brogue is an Irish or Scottish lilt, and also a sturdy punched-leather shoe.

clue.text: In the hotel finally was mischievous

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone misbehaved at the hotel at last.
explanation.definitionFit: Elfin can mean impish and mischievous, like a sprite.

clue.text: Carrots he produced for the old worker

indicators.note: the letters of 'carrots he' are produced in a new order

explanation.surface: A man brings out carrots for a tired old horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy draught horse is a traditional farm worker, often one past its prime.

clue.text: Either way make an allusion

indicators.note: the word reads identically from either direction, forwards or backwards

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Whichever way you go, mention something indirectly.
explanation.definitionFit: To refer to something is to mention or allude to it.

clue.text: Helping 'as to make notes about being first

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the singing word goes around another piece

parts.note: to sing is to produce musical notes
1st is written first; in crosswords the figure 1 is read as the letter I

explanation.surface: Someone helps by taking notes about who came first.
explanation.walkthrough: IST is 1ST with the figure one read as letter I; 'being' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Assisting means giving aid or support, the present participle like helping.

clue.text: Plain clothes must half fit casually

indicators.note: only the first half of the word must is taken
the word fit is rearranged in a casual, careless way

explanation.surface: Off-duty dress has to fit only loosely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' takes MU from MUST; 'casually' turns FIT into FTI.
explanation.definitionFit: Mufti is civilian dress worn by someone normally in uniform.

clue.text: A narrow rule that is not usually rigid

definitions.text: A narrow rule that is not usually rigid

parts.words: A narrow rule that is not usually rigid
parts.note: rule reads like a strict regulation but means a measuring strip, here a flexible one

explanation.surface: A strict regulation that is surprisingly lenient.
explanation.definitionFit: A flexible tape marked in units is a ruler that bends rather than staying stiff.
